mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real interest rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: financial crisis or emergency easing episode
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 0.5% in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) within a month signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +0.5% AND RSAFS > previous month +0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate of more than 0.4 percentage points from the previous month during a period when the federal funds rate is below 2% signals deteriorating labor market conditions in a low-rate environment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase of at least 0.8% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply expansion, which typically supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.8% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
